high.title: Securities Firm Unexpectedly Cuts VN-Index Forecast
high.summary: KB Securities Vietnam (KBSV) has revised its 2026 market outlook downward due to Middle East tensions affecting Vietnam's macroeconomic backdrop. KBSV cut its full-year EPS growth forecast for the entire market from 15.7% to 11% YoY, reflecting increased caution over geopolitical risks in the Middle East that are pressuring inflation, exchange rates, and interest rates. Additional headwinds include persistent liquidity shortages in the banking system and continued real estate credit controls. Despite the downward revision, double-digit earnings growth is still considered relatively positive given the government's economic stimulus policies. This forecast adjustment signals potential volatility ahead for Vietnamese equities and suggests fund managers should prepare for a more challenging environment than initially anticipated for 2026.

high.title: USD Exchange Rate, Deposit Interest Rate, and Banking System Liquidity Outlook for Q2/2026
high.summary: Vietcombank Securities (VCBS) reports continued USD/VND exchange rate pressure in Q1/2026. The central rate declined 19 VND to 25,102 VND/USD compared to end-Q4/2025, while commercial bank rates also dropped 20 VND to 26,357 VND/USD. However, the free market rate surged 520 VND to 26,920 VND/USD by end-Q1. Exchange rate pressures intensified in March amid concerns over Fed policy delays and rising geopolitical risks strengthening USD's safe-haven appeal. The State Bank of Vietnam deployed 180-day forward USD sales at 26,850 VND/USD to credit institutions to manage pressure. This divergence between official and free market rates, combined with SBV intervention, indicates ongoing FX volatility that international investors should monitor closely for potential VND weakness and bond market implications.

high.title: Total Market Margin Outstanding Hits New Record, Multiple Securities Firms Lend Over $1 Billion
high.summary: Vietnam's securities lending market reached new highs in Q1/2026, with total outstanding loans (including margin and advance selling) estimated at 415,000 billion VND, up 9,000 billion VND from end-2025. Margin lending specifically hit 405,000 billion VND, increasing 13,000 billion VND in just one quarter - the highest level in Vietnamese securities market history. Fifteen securities firms now have outstanding loans exceeding 10,000 billion VND, with five firms (TCBS, SSI, VPBankS, VPS, HSC) lending over $1 billion each. TCBS leads with nearly 45,000 billion VND outstanding. This surge in margin lending indicates strong investor confidence and liquidity in the equity market, potentially supporting continued VN-Index performance. However, the rapid growth in leverage also presents systemic risk considerations for market stability if sentiment turns negative.

medium.title: Dragon Capital Comments on Recent VN-Index Volatility
medium.summary: Dragon Capital reported VN-Index fell 11.9% MoM in March (USD terms) amid global market corrections due to geopolitical risks. Daily trading volume maintained around $1.3 billion supported by domestic flows while foreign flows remained mixed. The broad-based correction reflected general risk-off sentiment rather than fundamental weakness, with the index stabilizing by month-end.

medium.title: Mirae Asset Director: Market Correction is Good for "Refreshing" Capital Flows, 3 Stock Groups May Lead
medium.summary: Mirae Asset's Director Tran Quoc Toan noted positive market momentum with strong correlation between index performance and liquidity. Large-cap stocks leading the market suggests establishment of a more sustainable price foundation. VN-Index maintains good upward momentum heading into the new trading week, driven by Q1/2026 earnings expectations.

medium.title: This Week Banks Hold Shareholder Meetings in Succession: 6 Banks Meet on Same Day
medium.summary: Banking sector's AGM season peaks this week with multiple banks holding shareholder meetings. April 24 is the busiest day with six major banks (HDBank, TPBank, Vietcombank, VietinBank, BIDV, MSB) hosting AGMs simultaneously. State-owned giants will hold meetings at major Hanoi venues, indicating important strategic announcements and dividend decisions ahead.

medium.title: Are Banks Short of Money?
medium.summary: About 30 commercial banks reduced deposit rates from April 10, with cuts of 0.1-0.5%. Interbank VND rates also dropped significantly across all tenors, with overnight rates falling 2% to 4% annually. Despite rate cuts, banks still compete intensively for retail deposits, suggesting continued funding pressures in the system.

medium.title: Before AGM, Sacombank Suddenly "Reverses Course" and Cancels Restructuring Plan Extension Proposal
medium.summary: Sacombank's Board of Directors cancelled its proposal to extend the post-merger restructuring plan, citing ongoing challenges in NPL resolution and asset recovery. The bank continues comprehensive restructuring to improve operational efficiency and risk management capabilities.
